title: Inauguration of the U.P. Film Center
description: Formal inauguration of the U.P. Film Center Fine Arts Complex, featuring speeches of Imelda Marcos, awards, and recognition of leading Filipino filmmakers.
full_description: The formal inauguration of the U.P. Film Center Fine Arts Complex marked the opening of the University of the Philippines Film Center’s dedicated facilities and its establishment as a major institutional venue for film education, exhibition, production, research, and cultural activities. Imelda Romualdez-Marcos was invited to the inaugural event, while writer and filmmaker Virginia R. Moreno delivered a speech. Three young Filipino filmmakers—Lino Brocka, Ishmael Bernal, and Eddie Romero—were presented with awards during the ceremony. In lieu of the customary cornerstone, an antique jar containing a film reel and a painter’s palette was buried as the inauguration’s ceremonial foundation object. The ritual symbolized cinema’s relationship with earlier artistic traditions and expressed the idea that modern cinema could serve both as a user and preserver of older arts and of life itself. Following its inauguration, the Film Center operated as a central workshop for cinematic studies, developed the beginnings of a film research archive, and served as a showcase theater for Filipino and international cinema. The event consequently marked an important moment in the institutional establishment of film as an academic, artistic, archival, and cultural practice at the University of the Philippines.

title: Gala Premiere of The Story of Adele H., 80 Years of French Cinema
description: Gala benefit premiere of The Story of Adele H. celebrating 80 years of French cinema and supporting young filmmakers.
full_description:
The U.P. Film Center, in collaboration with the French Embassy, the Writers’ Union of the Philippines, and the Manila Film Society, presented a gala benefit premiere of François Truffaut’s The Story of Adele H., starring Isabelle Adjani, at the Rizal Theater on September 7, 1976. The event formed part of the celebration of 80 Years of French Cinema and was organized in support of the Young Filmmakers’ Fellowship Fund to France.

The gala brought together representatives of the Philippine and French cultural communities, filmmakers, writers, artists, patrons, and other supporters of cinema. It highlighted the U.P. Film Center’s role in presenting significant international films to Philippine audiences while fostering cultural exchange and connections between Filipino and French cinema.

The program included institutional and diplomatic messages, including those of Imelda Romualdez Marcos and Guy de Lestrange, Ambassadeur de France aux Philippines, as well as commentaries on the film and filmmaking by Filipino writers, poets, filmmakers, and film practitioners. Among those represented were Virginia R. Moreno, Adrian Cristobal, Jorge Arago, Ishmael Bernal, Romeo Vitug, Beatriz Romualdez-Francia, and U.P. Film Center archivist Annela Mendoza.

The event also acknowledged its patrons and institutional supporters, including Banque Nationale de Paris and Services Franco-Belges. Beyond its presentation of Truffaut’s film, the gala demonstrated the U.P. Film Center’s broader cultural and educational mission: to promote film appreciation, facilitate international cultural exchange, and support the development of Filipino filmmakers through opportunities for training and fellowship abroad.
